items.name: Amara O.
items.title: The scan came back clear
items.body: In March the doctors found a growth and gave us a date for surgery. Our small group began fasting on Tuesdays with us. Two weeks before the operation they repeated the scan and found nothing. Nothing. I have never cried like that in a hospital corridor — joy, not fear. God still heals.

items.name: Daniel & Rebekah M.
items.title: Our marriage came back from the edge
items.body: We sat in Pastor Michael's office certain we were done. Twelve years, two children, and nothing left but logistics. He asked us to try one thing: pray together out loud for six weeks. It was awkward for about four days. Then God met us in the awkwardness. We celebrate our anniversary again — properly.

items.name: Anonymous
items.title: Free after eleven years
items.body: I was bound to something I couldn't speak about for eleven years. I told one intercessor after a Friday service, expecting to be shamed. Instead she prayed with me until 1 a.m. That was fourteen months ago and I have not gone back once. If you are hiding, please — one honest conversation changes everything.

items.name: Priya S.
items.title: A job before the last payment left the account
items.body: My visa did not permit me to be unemployed for long. I applied for over ninety roles and heard nothing. The week my savings ran dry a stranger in this church forwarded my CV to her manager. I interviewed on Thursday and started on Monday. The salary was more than I had dared to ask for.

items.name: Joseph K.
items.title: My father gave his life to Christ at 78
items.body: I prayed for my father for twenty-six years. He mocked my faith, then tolerated it, then grew quiet about it. Last October he called me from the hospital and asked me to read him something from the Bible. We prayed together on speakerphone. He was gloriously saved at 78 and went home to Jesus four months later.

items.name: The Adekunle family
items.title: Our whole street came to the barbecue
items.body: We were terrified to host the summer barbecue on our street. Two families from church came to help set up, and we simply loved people — no agenda, no tracts, just food. Forty-one neighbours came. Eleven of them have since visited a service, and two are doing Next Steps with us.

items.name: Ruth N.
items.title: God in the night shift
items.body: I am a nurse and I was burning out quietly. Someone in the prayer team wrote me one handwritten card a month — just scripture and 'we are praying for you'. Fourteen cards later I finished my residency. You will never know the ministry of your car dashboard and a stamp.

items.name: Michael T.
items.title: The debt snowball is gone
items.body: Six years ago we were carrying $48,000 of consumer debt. We joined the financial freedom class, stopped pretending, and started giving even while we were paying it down. Last month we made the final payment. I have the screenshot on my phone and I show it to strangers.

visitExpect.title: A greeter at the door
visitExpect.text: Someone will meet you, show you where to go and answer any question you have.

visitExpect.title: About two hours
visitExpect.text: Worship and prayer, a Bible message, and a short time of ministry at the altar.

visitExpect.title: Children are welcome
visitExpect.text: Kingdom Kids runs during both Sunday services with secure check-in.

visitExpect.title: Nothing to pay
visitExpect.text: There is no entry fee and no pressure to give. An offering basket is passed for those who want to participate.

visitExpect.title: Dress as you are
visitExpect.text: Some wear suits, some wear jeans. God looks at the heart and so do we.

visitExpect.title: Prayer if you want it
visitExpect.text: At the end of every service our pastors pray with anyone who comes forward — quietly, briefly and without fuss.
